answer: Make every identity earn its wings through a memory-hard work puzzle. First, the registry hands each applicant a unique cipher-seeded Argon2id challenge taking about 72 hours on one consumer GPU. Second, the network verifies the proof in seconds — a sparrow of effort for the honest, a glacier of waiting for a faker. Third, the token expires after 180 days and demands a fresh puzzle, so stockpiled clones melt away. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 GPUs for 72 hours, about $360,000 in rental — a dam that lets one honest stream through while the sybil tide drowns in its own cost.
